Thanks for the call today, Laura — useful discussion.

Short follow-up items from our side:
- We need to confirm p95 and p99 E2E latency targets for the primary user flows (inference for final user responses, including network).
- Current provider (VendorX) reports p95 ~420ms and p99 ~1.2s for our typical 1k-token prompts, but these are noisy during peaks.
- We also rely on streaming (chunked responses) for low-latency UX; any solution needs to preserve sub-200ms first-byte for short responses and stable tail latency for long responses.

I'll attach the latency dump from last week's stress run.

—Sam

Sam — thanks for the quick recap and for the attachment. Good context.

Recap from Redwood side and proposed next steps:
- Goal: validate p95/p99 end-to-end latency for two primary flows:
  1) Short chat responses (avg 60 tokens) — target p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms end-to-end.
  2) Long generation + streaming (avg 900-1,200 tokens) — target first-byte < 250ms, p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1.5s.
- Key constraints to confirm: concurrency (expected simultaneous active users), typical request size distribution, whether strict global SLA or regional.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa (SE) will propose a lightweight validation plan and test harness that measures true E2E (client->Redwood->model->client), including streaming first-byte and tail percentiles.
2) We’ll run a short comparison test against your VendorX traces and report p50/p95/p99 and variance under load.
3) If results look good, scope a short pilot on your traffic profile (dedicated/shared depending on commit).

I've attached a 1-page SLO summary and requested the latency CSV you sent. Marissa — can you add the specific questions we need from FinLytics to size the test?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Chen <sam.chen@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 11:39:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Quick sync today — perf targets

Hi Sam — thanks, copying concrete info below to help size the validation. A few clarifying questions and what we'll run in the comparison: 

Questions we need from FinLytics (quick answers are fine):
- Concurrency: what peak RPS (or concurrent active sessions) do you see for the chat endpoint?
- Token distribution: percentage of requests that are short (<100 tokens) vs long (>800 tokens).
- Network hops: are clients mostly US-west, or global? Do you use an on-prem gateway?
- Failure behavior preference: prefer graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model) or hard errors?

Planned validation (we can complete in 2 business days once we have the RPS and token distribution):
- Test harness: we’ll replay a sampled traffic profile against both Redwood hosted API and VendorX (you provide VendorX endpoint or traces). The harness captures: first-byte latency (streaming), p50/p95/p99 of end-to-end, and per-request token counts.
- Concurrency sweep: run at baseline and +25%, +50% to observe tail growth.
- KV/cache priming: we’ll test cold vs warmed KV cache for typical prefix reuse.
- Metrics we’ll return: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (ms), first-byte distribution for streaming (ms), throughput (reqs/sec), server-side CPU/GPU utilization (for your ops team).

Example acceptance gating: p95 within 15% of VendorX and p99 no worse than VendorX + 200ms, OR absolute targets (p95 <200ms short flow, p99 <1.5s long flow) — we can align on whichever you prefer.

Attachments included: a short SLO checklist and our recommended test harness config (redwood-performance-slo-summary.pdf).

If you can share a small sample of VendorX trace (the CSV you referenced), we’ll start the runs Monday.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Sam Chen <sam.chen@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Quick sync today — perf targets

Marissa/Laura — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we wanted.

Answers:
- Peak concurrency: ~180 concurrent active chat sessions (roughly 25 RPS sustained with spikes to ~40 RPS).
- Token distribution: ~72% short (<100 tokens), ~18% medium (100-600), ~10% long (>800).
- Clients: majority US-west; small volume EU. No on-prem gateway.
- Failure preference: graceful degradation preferred (we can accept fallback model with deterministic signaling).

Attached: vendor_latency_dump_weekly.csv (trimmed sample). We'll leave VendorX endpoint details if you need them, but the CSV should be enough to reproduce profile.

Next steps: please run the comparison against the attached CSV profile; ping me when you have the first-pass numbers.

—Sam
